## Bottom Line

Netflix's **blended global ARM (Average Revenue per Membership) rose only modestly** — from **$10.82/month in 2019 to ~$11.70/month in 2024, about +8% over five years** (and just +5.7% on a Q4-to-Q4 basis: $11.06 → $11.69).

That's a striking result given how aggressively Netflix raised prices. The explanation is **geographic mix shift**: growth came overwhelmingly from lower-priced APAC and LATAM, which diluted the global average. Regionally, the picture is wildly divergent.

---

## Reported ARM, Q4 2019 vs. Q4 2024 (monthly, USD)

| Region | Q4 2019 | Q4 2024 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| **UCAN** (US/Canada) | $13.22 | $17.26 | **+30.6%** |
| **EMEA** | $10.51 | $11.11 | +5.7% |
| **LATAM** | $8.18 | $8.00 | **−2.2%** |
| **APAC** | $9.07 | $7.34 | **−19.1%** |
| **Global blended** | **$11.06** | **$11.69** | **+5.7%** |

## Full-Year ARM, 2019 vs. 2024

| Region | FY2019 | FY2024 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| UCAN | $12.57 | ~$17.20 | +37% |
| EMEA | $10.33 | ~$10.96 | +6% |
| LATAM | $8.21 | ~$8.24 | flat |
| APAC | $9.24 | ~$7.29 | −21% |
| **Global** | **$10.82** | **~$11.70** | **+8%** |

*(Global FY2024 = $39,001M streaming revenue ÷ ~277.7M average paid memberships ÷ 12. Netflix ceased disclosing ARM after Q4 2024, so 2024 is the final data point.)*

---

## Why the blended number barely moved

1. **Mix shift to low-ARM markets.** APAC went from 9.7% to 19.1% of global members (membership nearly quadrupled from 16M to 58M), while UCAN fell from 40.5% to 29.7% of members. Every APAC member adds ~$7/month vs. ~$17 in UCAN, dragging the average down.

2. **FX headwinds.** The strong dollar crushed reported ARM in LATAM and APAC. On an **F/X-neutral basis**, LATAM ARM actually grew ~16–27% per quarter in 2024, and APAC was only modestly negative — the reported dollar figures mask real local-currency pricing gains.

3. **Cheaper plan tiers.** The ad-supported tier and mobile-only plans in emerging markets lowered revenue per membership by design, trading ARPU for volume.

4. **Total memberships grew +80% (167M → 302M)**, so while ARM per user grew only ~8%, total streaming revenue more than doubled ($19.9B → $39.0B).

**Net effect:** The headline "ARM" number understates Netflix's pricing power — in its mature, high-value markets (UCAN) ARM rose ~30–37%, while the blended figure is held back by deliberate expansion into lower-ARPU, high-growth regions and currency translation.
